commits.edited_message:
Improve performance of decodeAi7Thumbnail.

Preallocate the expanded RGB buffer and write pixels directly instead of
appending to a string. The fill loop bounds itself with width*height*3,
the same geometric size ai7ThumbnailSize() returns as expectedSize.

Avoid unsigned comparison warning

Promote the AI7 run length to size_t before multiplying by the bytes per
pixel, so the comparison against the remaining buffer is unsigned.

Widths above 16 bits include a trailing sentinel column that is not part
of the stored thumbnail. Drop that column when computing the expanded RGB
allocation.

coupling: decodeAi7Thumbnail's fill loop and ai7ThumbnailSize() start out describing the same buffer. c5a074c stops using the size helper's expectedSize as the loop bound and instead recomputes width*height*3. That is safe on its own: at that commit ai7ThumbnailSize() returns exactly width*height*3, the DataBuf is allocated to expectedSize, and a thumbnail whose pixel count matches the declared geometry fills the buffer and passes the length check. 013696f only promotes the run-length multiply to size_t and, in ai7ThumbnailSize(), drops one column when width exceeds 16 bits before computing the allocation. On the original decoder that still bounds the fill by expectedSize, the shorter allocation and the loop agree, and a longer payload is rejected with kerCorruptedMetadata before any store. The overflow appears only when both are present. For a 65536x1 AI7 thumbnail the size helper allocates (65536-1)*3 bytes while the fill loop still writes 65536*3 bytes, so the last pixel's three stores run past the DataBuf. Neither diff is an out-of-bounds write against the parent it was written for; the bug is the disagreement between the geometric bound introduced in the first commit and the shortened allocation introduced in the second. Repairing only the unsigned cast, or only the way the fill loop is written, leaves that disagreement in place. The sizes have to be reconciled across the two commits.
